stories.headline: Yoba Malware Disguised as ChatGPT and Claude Desktop Apps
stories.summary: Check Point researchers have uncovered a new malware campaign dubbed 'Yoba,' which distributes cryptocurrency miners through fake desktop versions of popular AI models like ChatGPT and Claude hosted on GitHub. This sophisticated attack leverages the high demand for local AI interfaces to trick users into installing malicious software.
stories.original_title: [Help Net Security] Yoba malware hides in fake desktop versions of ChatGPT and Claude
stories.context: Imagine if someone put a virus inside a popular video game download; that is essentially what this malware campaign does, but with artificial intelligence programs. Hackers created fake versions of well-known AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude, hiding them on GitHub, which is a website where programmers share code and software. Because people are so eager to use these powerful AI assistants on their own computers, they lower their guard and install the files without checking if they are safe. Once installed, the "virus" secretly uses your computer’s power to mine cryptocurrency for the hackers, slowing down your device and stealing energy without you knowing it.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows how hackers are using our love for new AI tools to steal money. If you download a fake app thinking it is safe, your computer might secretly work for criminals instead of you. It proves that being careful about where you get software is just as important as protecting your passwords.
stories.other_side: Some people argue that users should be more careful and check sources before downloading anything. They believe blaming the developers takes away personal responsibility for keeping devices secure.

stories.headline: Oracle Targets 10GW AI Compute Capacity Amid $664B Backlog
stories.summary: Oracle has announced an ambitious plan to reach 10 gigawatts of AI compute capacity by fiscal year 2028, driven by a massive backlog of $664 billion. This expansion aims to solidify its position in the competitive AI infrastructure market, though success depends heavily on timely execution and delivery of necessary hardware.
stories.original_title: [Crypto Briefing] Oracle targets 10GW of AI compute by FY28 as its backlog hits $664 billion
stories.context: Artificial intelligence requires massive amounts of computing power, which comes from specialized chips and data centers that consume huge amounts of electricity. Oracle is a major company that rents out this computing power to other businesses, but right now there is a shortage of available space, leading to a backlog of orders worth hundreds of billions of dollars. To fix this, they are planning a massive construction project to build enough infrastructure to handle ten gigawatts of power, which is roughly equivalent to the electricity used by several large cities. This expansion is crucial because if they cannot deliver the hardware fast enough, their customers might switch to competitors who can meet the growing demand for AI services.
stories.why_it_matters: Oracle is betting big that every company will need huge amounts of computing power for AI soon. If they pull this off, they could control a massive part of the internet's brainpower. This means faster AI tools for everyone, but also higher costs if not enough people buy their services.
stories.other_side: Critics say building all this hardware is risky and expensive. If companies do not actually need that much power, Oracle could lose billions on empty data centers.

stories.headline: DoorDash Acquires Instacart in Record $17 Billion Deal
stories.summary: DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart for approximately $17 billion, creating a dominant force in the US delivery sector by combining two major platforms. The deal is expected to face intense regulatory and antitrust scrutiny as it merges leading rivals in food and grocery delivery services.
stories.original_title: [Ibtimes.com.au] DoorDash Strikes $17 Billion Deal to Buy Instacart, Uniting Delivery Rivals in Its Biggest Bet on Groceries
stories.context: For years, DoorDash has been the go-to app for ordering restaurant food, while Instacart has dominated the market for grocery delivery, meaning they rarely competed directly for the same meals. By buying Instacart for $17 billion, DoorDash aims to become the single largest delivery service in the United States, covering everything from dinner ingredients to household supplies. However, combining two such powerful rivals raises serious concerns among government regulators who worry that one company controlling too much of the market could raise prices and treat workers unfairly. This type of merger often faces intense legal scrutiny to ensure that competition remains healthy for consumers and small business owners alike.
stories.why_it_matters: Merging DoorDash and Instacart creates one giant delivery company that controls almost all food and grocery orders. This could mean fewer choices for customers and higher prices since there is less competition. It changes how we shop by putting too much power in one pair of hands.
stories.other_side: Supporters claim combining these services makes deliveries faster and cheaper for shoppers. They argue that a bigger company can invest more in better technology and driver pay.

stories.headline: Anthropic Co-founder Christopher Olah Set for Multibillion-Dollar Windfall from IPO
stories.summary: Christopher Olah, a Canadian dropout and co-founder of AI safety firm Anthropic, is poised to make billions as the company prepares for its initial public offering. This event highlights the significant financial opportunities emerging within the generative AI sector and the valuation of key figures in AI development.
stories.original_title: [Financial Post] Meet the Canadian dropout set to reap a multibillion-dollar windfall from Anthropic’s IPO
stories.context: An initial public offering, or IPO, is when a private company sells shares to the public for the first time, allowing early employees and founders to cash in on their hard work. Christopher Olah is a co-founder of Anthropic, a firm focused on making artificial intelligence safe and reliable, rather than just making it faster or more profitable. As his company prepares to go public, the value of the business skyrockets, turning his personal stake into billions of dollars. This situation highlights how the current boom in generative AI is creating unprecedented wealth for the key scientists and leaders driving these new technologies forward.
stories.why_it_matters: This story highlights how rich the founders of AI companies are becoming very quickly. It shows that building smart machines is turning into one of the most profitable industries in history. This wealth shift may influence who gets to decide how AI is used in the future.
stories.other_side: Some worry that focusing so much on making billionaires richer distracts from the real work of making AI safe. They fear that profit motives might push companies to release dangerous tools too early.

stories.headline: India's AI Investment Boom Expands Beyond IT Sector
stories.summary: India is experiencing a surge in AI investment that extends beyond traditional IT services into power, data centers, and electronics manufacturing. Experts suggest this diversification offers sustainable earnings growth opportunities, signaling a broader technological infrastructure build-out across the country.
stories.original_title: [Livemint] AI investment boom in India: Which sectors beyond IT could benefit from data centres, power and electronics growth?
stories.context: India has long been known as a global hub for information technology services, such as customer support and software coding, but its economy is now expanding into the physical building blocks of AI. The country is investing heavily in constructing the actual infrastructure needed for AI, including power plants, data centers, and factories that make electronic components. This shift is significant because it moves India beyond just providing labor or services to becoming a central player in manufacturing the hardware that powers the digital world. Experts believe this diversification will lead to steady economic growth and create a more resilient technology sector less dependent on traditional IT outsourcing.
stories.why_it_matters: India is moving beyond just writing code to building the actual physical infrastructure for AI. This growth creates jobs and modernizes the country’s power grid and factories. It signals that AI development is spreading globally, not just staying in the US or China.
stories.other_side: Environmental groups worry that building so many data centers will use too much electricity and water. They fear this rapid expansion could harm local communities and increase pollution.

stories.headline: New MacBook Pro Features OLED Display and Enhanced Hardware
stories.summary: The latest MacBook Pro introduces an OLED display alongside other significant upgrades including a lighter design, improved speakers, and increased storage options. However, these advanced features come with a $400 premium compared to standard models, marking a substantial shift in Apple's laptop hardware strategy.
stories.original_title: [Cult of Mac] OLED MacBook Pro vs. regular MacBook Pro: It’s not just about the screen
stories.context: Apple recently updated its high-end laptops, introducing an OLED screen, which offers deeper blacks and brighter colors compared to the older LCD screens found in previous models. These improvements come at a steep price, adding $400 to the cost of the device, which reflects Apple's strategy of charging a premium for cutting-edge technology. While the new design is lighter and has better speakers, the significant price hike forces buyers to decide if the visual and audio upgrades are worth the extra expense. This move signals a broader trend in the tech industry where manufacturers are pushing higher-quality displays and hardware to justify increased costs for professional users and enthusiasts.
stories.why_it_matters: Apple is making laptops look better but forcing users to pay extra for basic features like high-quality screens. This pushes people to spend more money to keep their computers useful for years. It sets a trend where other tech companies might start charging for things we once got for free.
stories.other_side: Fans argue that the new screen and design make the laptop worth the extra cost because it lasts longer. They believe paying more upfront saves money over time by avoiding frequent replacements.
